header: Date: 2026-10-02 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes\nAttendees: Sarah Kim (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Maria Lopez (Accolade Procurement), David Chen (Accolade Legal), Priya Nair (CTO), Ben Torres (Eng Manager), Oliver King (Security)
summary: Procurement and legal call to review MSA/DPA, SLAs and pricing approval path. Redwood AE/SE walked through standard MSA/DPA language, SLA targets and escalation, and onboarding timeline. Customer raised data residency and encryption/KMS questions and requested redlines around liability and breach notification timelines. Agreement on next steps: Redwood to deliver redlines, SE to prepare onboarding checklist and SSO details, Accolade to confirm PO timeline.
topics: DPA data residency and breach notification
SLA targets and credits (99.9% / support tiers)
transcript:
00:00 Sarah Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll give a quick agenda - MSA/DPA, SLAs, pricing timeline and onboarding notes.
00:14 Maria Lopez: Thanks Sarah, we have procurement and legal on the line to get this across the finish line.
00:22 Raj Patel: Hi all, Raj from Redwood SE, I'll run the technical bits on SSO, KMS, and VPC options.
00:30 David Chen: Great, I'll jump in on the DPA stuff and liability questions.
00:38 Sarah Kim: Cool, first on MSA - standard term sheet we sent last week, main asks we've seen are liability cap adjustments and termination for convenience windows. Our standard cap is 3x the fees, we can discuss.
00:55 David Chen: The legal team prefers a limited cap tied to fees but want narrower carveouts for IP indemnity and personal data breaches. Also we need a clear 72 hour breach notification window.
01:12 Sarah Kim: We can commit to 72 hours for incident notification in the DPA. For liability, we usually do 3x fees or USD 1M floor, would that be a blocker?
01:30 Ben Torres: For procurement's budgeting we need predictability - if the floor is too low our legal may push back. Can we get an exception if we commit to a multi-year term?
01:42 Sarah Kim: Yes, we can discuss term-based concessions - Lena from CSM can outline enterprise discounts for a 12-24 month commit.
01:52 Lena Ortiz: Happy to, I can send a pricing sheet after the call.
02:00 Priya Nair: On the SLA side, what are your uptime and latency targets for our expected workload? We're doing multi-regional customer-facing chat.
02:10 Raj Patel: For hosted API our standard SLA is 99.9% monthly availability for production endpoints with support tiers - dedicated offers stronger SLOs and isolation. Latency depends on model and config; we can show perf profiles.
02:26 Priya Nair: Is there an SLA credit schedule? We need that documented for our procurement team.
02:33 Sarah Kim: Yes, SLA credits are in the SLA exhibit - typically service credits scaled by downtime buckets, e.g., <99.9% get X% credit, <99.0% higher credits. We'll include the exact table in the SLA exhibit in the redline.
02:49 Oliver King: Two security questions: do you support customer-managed KMS, and can audit logs be exported to our SIEM? Also data residency - we need EU only for certain customers.
03:02 Raj Patel: We support customer-managed keys for Private deployments and integrations with common KMS vendors. Audit logs export is available via our Console and SIEM webhooks; we'll include the API endpoints in the onboarding doc. For EU-only data residency we can offer region pinning; for stricter requirements Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) is an option.
03:25 Maria Lopez: Procurement asks: what's the approval cadence for pricing? We need an approved discount and a PO date to align with our quarter close.
03:33 Sarah Kim: If you sign a 12 month commit there is a standard enterprise discount tier; I can get legal and finance to provide the exact discount table. For PO we typically ask for a signed MSA and PO - timeline depends on your internal approvals.
03:50 David Chen: On DPA specifics - subprocessor list, data deletion timelines, and cross-border transfer mechanisms. We want to ensure subprocessors are notified and a right to audit clause.
04:05 Raj Patel: We maintain a subprocessors list in the security pack, and we can add notification commitments. Right to audit is typically handled via SOC2 reports and audit rights in the enterprise package.
04:18 Ben Torres: A practical question - how long is onboarding from signed MSA to prod traffic? We need an estimate.
04:26 Raj Patel: For hosted API it's usually a couple of days for API keys and integration, but for dedicated or private deployments plan for 4-6 weeks for capacity provisioning, network setup and SSO. We'll share a detailed checklist.
04:43 Maria Lopez: Any blockers from our side we should know - we need legal to see redlines quickly.
04:48 Sarah Kim: We'll send redlined MSA/DPA with SLA exhibit and pricing appendix by Monday 2026-10-05.
04:55 David Chen: Good. Also want to confirm indemnity language for third party claims, we'll flag exact language in comments.
05:03 Sarah Kim: Noted, we'll call out IP indemnity carveouts.
05:07 Priya Nair: One more - are there limits on model customization or private weights? Because we evaluate on-prem for sensitive use cases.
05:16 Raj Patel: We support model weights on private deployments and allow pinned model versions. We'll include the options and tradeoffs (performance/cost) in the doc.
05:29 Maria Lopez: Regarding pricing approvals - can you provide a one-page summary that procurement can circulate?
05:35 Lena Ortiz: Absolutely, I'll prepare a one pager and the pricing sheet after the call.
05:40 Sarah Kim: Recap: Redwood sends redlined MSA/DPA, SLA exhibit and pricing appendix by 2026-10-05; Accolade reviews and confirms PO timeline by 2026-10-09; SE and Accolade eng to schedule onboarding week of 2026-10-12.
05:58 David Chen: We may push a few redlines but will aim to respond quickly.
06:04 Ben Torres: For the technical kick-off please include network diagrams and SSO guide.
06:10 Raj Patel: Will do - I'll include SAML samples and sample NGINX/ALB networking patterns for VPC peering.
06:19 Maria Lopez: Thanks everyone, that helps.
06:24 Sarah Kim: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the deck and security pack.
06:30 (end)
